beats.intent: ThinkSR keeps a dense carrier moving through encode, window, shared recurrent thought ticks, and decode.
beats.claim: ThinkSR end to end: encoder, windows, shared DQ-CTM ticks, decoder.
beats.narration: The method keeps dense spatial information available while a compact thought process reads and updates it. The encoder turns the low-resolution image into features. Windowing divides those features for local processing. The DQ-CTM thought process runs for repeated ticks with shared parameters. The decoder turns the updated dense field back into the super-resolved image. Recurrence returns to the thought stage itself, so the whole pipeline is not rerun each tick.

params.headline: ThinkSR runs dense features through shared thought ticks
params.note: Persistent dense carrier read and updated by compact thought.

beats.intent: The carrier starts as encoder features, then window partitioning forms tokens without dropping the dense field.
beats.claim: A persistent dense carrier, read and updated by a compact thought process.
beats.narration: The carrier equation defines the dense state before the thought process touches it. The encoder maps the low-resolution input into a dense feature field. The window partition operates on that field, preserving every token for the next stage.

params.headline: The dense carrier is encoded first, then windowed

beats.intent: DQ-CTM-SR is not the smallest model; at 1.129 million parameters, it is second largest among the five listed methods.
beats.claim: Table 1 reports Params: CATANet 0.535M, RFDN 0.550M, IMDN 0.715M, DQ-CTM-SR 1.129M, CARN 1.592M.
beats.narration: The parameter counts put DQ-CTM-SR closer to the large end of this group. CATANet is the smallest reported model. RFDN is only slightly larger. IMDN sits in the middle. DQ-CTM-SR reaches one point one two nine million parameters, making it the second largest of the five. CARN remains the largest model in the comparison.
